newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania artists make campaign noise over copyright.
newsitem.headline: Romania artists make campaign noise over copyright.

text.p: Two composers determined to prevent their songs being borrowed for electioneering jingles have filed complaints against their use in Romania's election campaign, an official said on Thursday.
Radu Clondescu, copyright expert at the Union of Romanian Composers, said the musicians had protested over alleged violation of tough copyright rules adopted earlier this year.
"Composer Ilie Stepan complained that a video in incumbent president Ion Iliescu's campaign was using soundbites from "The Meaning of Life', his latest album," Clondescu told Reuters.
He said Marius Dragomir had complained over the use of songs from his rock album, "Party in Transylvania", in the campaign of Liberal Radu Campeanu, one of several also-rans in the presidential race.
"The musicians just don't want their music to be part of the electoral campaign," Clondescu said.

Iliescu is vying for a new term against 15 challengers in presidential elections on November 3. Thousands of candidates are also competing for seats in parliament. Iliescu's campaign staff were unaware of copyright breaches in his videos, aired this week by both state and private television stations.
"But if it's true, the terms of the copyright law will have to be respected," Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu, a member of Iliescu's campaign, told Mediafax news agency.
Under the law, copyright violations carry jail terms of up to seven years and can trigger the loss of business licences.
The rules beefed up scant protection and brought Romania -- after Poland Eastern Europe's second largest market outside the former Soviet Union -- closer to Western practice.
Romania is on a U.S. Commerce Department "watch list" of countries with inadequate copyright and high piracy rates.
U.S. officials say up to 90 percent of the local computer software market is counterfeit, while counterfeit music tapes, compact discs and videotapes still dominate the local market.
